text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I ran a FP8 calibration sweep with the new sample policy and hit surprising p95 regressions on the inference fleet.
kevin: Can you paste the run config and the perf numbers?
maya: run: `./perf_run --model gpt-small --quant fp8 --calib calib_set_v3.json --batch 1`
result: p50 6.9ms, p95 12.3ms -> after calib p95 17.8ms (cold cache)
I can upload full trace.
sarah: Did you use per-channel or per-tensor calibration? That often flips which matmul kernel the selector picks.
maya: per-channel, with channel clipping at 3-sigma. The calib set intentionally included ~10% tail-domain docs (legal/finance) to stress outliers.
kevin: That tail shard probably increased unique prefix overlap -> worse KV cache reuse. If KV cache hit-rate drops you see extra memory fetches and different kernel tiling gets chosen.
sarah: We need the profiler flame. Also, which kernel variant did runtime pick? (`gemm_fp8_fast` vs `gemm_mixed_tile32`)
maya: perf-bot: job 8852 finished, profile url: https://s3.redwood/profiles/8852.flame
perf-bot: job 8852: kernel chosen = gemm_fp8_fast (fallback path engaged during long seqs)
kevin: Interesting. The fallback shows higher arithmetic intensity for cold KV access. Suggestion: separate calib objectives — accuracy delta + perf penalty on p95.
sarah: Agree. Per-tensor calibration tends to choose 'safer' scales that avoid per-channel extremes and often keep us on the lower-latency kernel, but it can cost a couple points of quality.
maya: Our product SLO is 15ms p95 for chat. Proposal: dual-calib approach: sample 80% production-like (user token distribution) + 20% heavy-tail stress set. Compute quant params for both and pick parameters that minimize score = p95_ms * 1.2 + max(0, quality_delta)*100.
kevin: That objective is fine but we should also test KV warmup scenarios: cold (no KV cache), steady (hot cache), and warmup ramp (first 50 tokens). Perf differences can be huge.
sarah: Also consider forbidding tail-only-induced kernel flips by feeding a synthesized `calib-profile.json` into kernel selector that biases towards production histograms.
maya: Implementation note: current selector accepts `--profile-overrides` with histograms. I can generate one from production traces and append the tail shard as separate bucket.
kevin: For experiment reproducibility, please include commands to replay: `python scripts/replay_workload.py --trace s3://traces/prod-sample --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --kv-warmup 0,16`.
perf-bot: scheduled matrix run 8853: batches [1,4,8], kv_warmup [0,16], kernels auto.
maya: Also observed accuracy: per-channel gave +0.6% perplexity vs per-tensor baseline, but latency hit was +4.5ms p95 on average. Hybrid (per-channel with global-clipping) cut the latency back by ~2ms and kept +0.4% perplexity.
sarah: Sounds like hybrid wins for our SLO. We should codify sampling: 80% prod, 15% heavy-tail, 5% adversarial long-prefixes.
kevin: One caveat: if we over-weight tail examples they'll force kernel selector to prefer fallback kernels for all seq lengths. We should clamp that by telling selector to respect the 80/20 weighting explicitly.
maya: I'll drop the new sets to s3://calib/experiments/stratified-hybrid-v1 and push a PR with repro steps.
ops-bot: calendar: calibration sync Wed 10:00am — invites sent to maya, kevin, sarah.
kevin: I'll run the perf matrix once artifacts land. Also will run a cold-start cluster with no KV snapshot to measure worst-case.
sarah: Great. After we pick the final params let's run a 24h canary on dedicated pool to check real traffic jitter.
maya: Thanks — uploading scripts now. TL;DR: favor hybrid per-channel with stratified sampling (80/20) and explicit profile overrides to avoid tail-driven kernel flips.
